comments.text: Reversing the batch doesn't fix the underlying stale-record problem, it only makes it depend on row order. The assumption that 'a record could reference only records that already exist' is false: records can be updated later to reference newer records (e.g. create c, then b, then update c to reference [a, b]); with the reversed order b is processed first, its cascade updates/deletes c in the DB, and then the stale in-memory c from the same batch is still processed and saved back, reintroducing the dangling reference. It also relies on the rows query having a deterministic creation-time order, which isn't guaranteed unless the query explicitly orders by it. The robust fix is to re-fetch each referencing record (or skip it if it no longer exists / was already processed) right before modifying or deleting it in deleteRefRecords. Please add a regression test for the self-referencing cascade case, including the 'updated later to reference a newer record' variant.
